newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY BILL AMENDED.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY BILL AMENDED.

text.p: The parliamentary trade and industry committee on Monday acted to limit the sweeping powers originally proposed for government officials examining intellectual property rights infringements.

Committee chairman Rob Davies said there had been concern that the Intellectual Property Laws Amendment Bill gave inspectors too wide authority to enter or search premises for counterfeit goods without warrants.
The committee accepted an amendment that would allow entry and search without warrants as long as warrants were obtained within 10 days.
It also introduced a clause that would ensure that people being investigated or questioned would be given the right to remain silent and informed of the consequences of remaining silent.

The committee broadened the definition of guilt to ensure that people found guilty of trade in counterfeit goods were aware that the goods were counterfeit rather than merely being in possession of them.

The bill, which is linked to the Counterfeit Goods Bill which the committee passed without amendment, is aimed at cracking down on the growing trade in counterfeit goods in South Africa since the lifting of sanctions. It is in line with the country's World Trade Organisation obligations.
